**The meaning of the verses**
﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِن جَاءَكُمْ فَاسِقٌ بِنَبَإٍ فَتَبَيَّنُوا أَن تُصِيبُوا قَوْمًا بِجَهَالَةٍ فَتُصْبِحُوا عَلَىٰ مَا فَعَلْتُمْ نَادِمِينَ﴾

O you who have believed in Allah and His Messenger and acted by His law: if a wicked person comes to you with news, verify his news before believing it and passing it on, until you know it is true; lest you harm innocent people through a wrong done by you, and then regret it.

﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اجْتَنِبُوا كَثِيرًا مِّنَ الظَّنِّ إِنَّ بَعْضَ الظَّنِّ إِثْمٌ﴾

O you who have believed in Allah and His Messenger and acted by His law: avoid much evil suspicion of the believers; some of that suspicion is a sin …

📖 At-Tafsir Al-Muyassar — King Fahd Complex.

**Talk with your child**
1. What did Mas'ud really see at sunset? And what did he tell the people? And what did his words become after passing from mouth to mouth?
2. What did Sheikh Hamid suggest? And why did they not follow his advice? And what would have changed if they had walked to Spring Village to ask, not to strike?
3. Does the verse mean that we should never believe anyone? (No; it means that we should make sure before we judge someone, pass on something about them, or hurt them because of news we have not checked.) And what question should the people sitting there have asked Mas'ud?

**This week's exercise**
Play the "whisper" game at home: the first person whispers a sentence to the one next to them, and so on to the last, then compare what arrived with what was first said. And all week, when your child brings news about someone, they ask themselves before telling it: Did I see it with my own eyes? Did I make sure?
